newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin hails end to Peru hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin hails end to Peru hostage crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday hailed the military end to Peru's four-month hostage crisis as a "unanimous rejection of terrorism," Interfax news agency said.

"The president believes it is exactly such a unanimous rejection of terrorism in any form that is the most effective barrier against terrorism," Iterfax quoted presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.
Peruvian troops on Tuesday freed 71 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home and killed all the rebel captors who seized the building on December 17.
The Russian foreign ministry applauded the leadership of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.
"The end of the operation, which was achieved through the skillful and cool-headed actions of the Peruvian authorities, was viewed with satisfaction and relief," the ministry said in a statement.
"Thanks to the coherent actions of President A. Fujimori and his uncompromising position towards terrorists...this barbaric act was cut short."
Russia has been plagued by a series of hostage-taking raids, several of which have prompted military intervention.
The use of force to try to end two hostage crises in southern Russia, in Pervomaiskoye in 1996 and Budennovsk in 1995, brought many civilian casualties.
